newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents higher Tuesday as traders expect prices to bounce back after the two-day sell-off.

Traders said forecasts calling for cooler temperatures in top-grower Brazil this weekend may also give the market a boost. Weather Services Corp said Tuesday that although temperatures are expected to turn colder over the weekend, no damaging cold is expected in Brazil's coffee belt.

Monday, New York arabica futures plummeted as speculators continued to take profits. July tumbled 22.45 cents to end at 253.95 cents a lb after ranging between 275.00 and 247.50. September slid 13.75 cents to 224.55 cents, while the back months finished 11.45 lower to 0.10 higher.
The July/September spread shrank to 29.40 cents from 38.10 cents at the close on Friday. September/December narrowed to 35.60 cents from 37.90 cents.
Technically, traders said July would find support at Monday's low of 247.50, while near-term resistance was seen at 260.00, followed by 275.00.

London robusta futures gapped $55 lower Tuesday, but managed to pare losses by midday. LIFFE July was down $25 at the break at $2,085 after bottoming at $2,026. Some New York traders said London's inability to reach its down $100 pre-opening call contributed to the CSCE higher call.
